paras: The Tarboro warehouse shooting was the shooting of an unnamed Black man by a Tarboro, North Carolina, policeman named Winborn in Capt. Brown's warehouse on a Tuesday night in early 1881. The man was said to have been stealing meat, and the only known account, a one-line item from the Tarboro Southerner, does not say whether he survived.

According to the Southerner, Policeman Winborn shot "a negro" inside Capt. Brown's warehouse at night. The item explained the shooting only with the words "stealing meat," giving the policeman's side of the encounter as plain fact. It named neither the man nor his injuries, and it did not describe how the encounter began or whether Winborn had tried to arrest him.
The item gave no calendar date, and because it reached Raleigh as a reprint published on Thursday, 10 February 1881, the "Tuesday night" may have been 1 or 8 February or earlier.
No report of an inquest, a charge against Winborn, or a prosecution of the man for theft appears in the coverage.

The shooting reached a wider readership through The Farmer and Mechanic of Raleigh, which reprinted the Southerner's sentence on 10 February 1881 in a column of state news. There it ran without a headline or comment, between an anecdote about a champion turkey hunter who killed five birds at one shot and notes on local residents leaving for Texas. The man appeared only as "a negro," and the theft accusation served as the whole explanation for the shooting.
No other newspaper account of the shooting has been found.
